html:
The Meskwaki, called the Fox by the French and English, are an Algonquian people of the western Great Lakes. In the 1600s they lived in what is now Wisconsin; the Fox River there is named after them.

They farmed maize in summer villages and hunted in winter. They stood apart from most of their neighbours by resisting New France, which wanted free passage through their lands for the fur trade. In the Fox Wars of 1712 to 1733 the French and their Native allies killed many Meskwaki. The survivors joined their close kin the Sauk, and the two peoples, Sauk and Meskwaki, moved south into Illinois and Iowa.

Some Meskwaki fought in the Black Hawk War of 1832. After removal to Kansas, a group came back and in 1857 bought land in Iowa. Their Meskwaki Settlement near Tama is still owned by the tribe; others live in Kansas and Oklahoma.
